newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended higher than New York's previous close on marginal amounts of shortcovering and stocking up by physical buyers ahead of the Easter weekend, dealers said on Tuesday.
"We saw bits and pieces of shortcovering, but most of the activity was bookkeeping," said a bullion dealer at a bank in the territory.
Bullion sources said physical buyers were stocking up ahead of the Easter weekend that runs from Friday to Monday.
"There was good buying below $350 per ounce," one bullion trader said.
Bullion ended at US$350.40/90 an ounce against New York's US$349.75/350.25 close on Monday.
Other traders said the market was quiet ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting arm, which will consider an interest rate hike.
Local gold ended HK$14 lower at HK$3,244 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -7.00 from its previous fix at nil.
